summary: Cytarabine carries the FDA's strongest boxed warning regarding blood-related harm, stomach or intestinal harm, and liver harm, and it requires treatment by experienced cancer doctors in facilities equipped to monitor patients [3][7]. The drug also has a warning for strongly suppressing bone marrow activity, which requires close medical supervision and blood cell count checks [7]. Additionally, results from a small computer model, rather than tests on people, gave it a high score for liver harm and a low score for heart harm [M]. Multiple clinical trials involving this drug have also stopped early due to safety concerns and dose-limiting toxicities [9][10][11].
